plateau.caveats: Daily capture decays from 2018-08-21 (extract artefact), so August is excluded or day-matched. The FIFA World Cup (14 Jun - 15 Jul 2018, Brazil playing) overlaps the weak Jun-Jul window; not tested.

stages_jan_mar_2018.method: distributional Shapley (rank-preserving quantile mapping of each stage)
stages_jan_mar_2018.reading: Positive = this stage's change raised the late rate.

recommendations.title: Split the survey: delivery-issue contact at promise + 2 days, star rating on confirmed delivery
recommendations.why: 70% of late orders are rated before they arrive.
recommendations.impact: removes ≤ 2,215 pre-delivery 1–2★ ratings/yr (≈1,866 with exact-day matching); value = rating accuracy, no BRL claimed
recommendations.confidence: High on direction, medium on size

recommendations.title: Don't roll out shorter promises; A/B a 3-day-capped lane-P80 after the peak
recommendations.why: Full year, lane-P80 saves 6.4 d but late rises 9.3% → 20.6%.
recommendations.impact: capped arm: −1.6 d, late 9.3% → 10.8% (full year); pays only above +0.032% conversion per day saved
recommendations.date: run 2019-01-14 → 2019-02-10 (after the peak and after #1), final read-out 2019-03-03

ab_design.unit: customer (cookie), 50/50, all lanes; treatment promise = max(lane-P80, current − 3 days)
ab_design.primary_metric: checkout conversion of sessions that saw a promise
ab_design.guardrail: matured late rate, treatment − control ≤ +3 pp (read after promise + 7 days)
ab_design.kill_metric: in-flight past-promise share (real time): stop if treatment − control > 3 pp for 3 consecutive days
ab_design.overrides_preset_rule: The pre-set rule rejects every capped arm (5-day cap: 17.6% late in Oct–Mar vs the 7% bar). Its own pick uses the 99th percentile in 7 of 11 months and lengthens promises by 7.5 days on average all year. Testing a capped cut is a judgement call that overrides the rule.
ab_design.conversion_mde_note: needs session counts (not in the extract): MDE ≈ 2.8·sqrt(2c(1−c)/S)

recommendations.title: Fix partial shipments: mark 'delivered' only when every item has arrived, and announce split shipments
recommendations.why: 'Incomplete order' is a top-two complaint on ON-TIME orders (23%, CI 19%–27%); 65% are multi-item orders (12% of reviews).
recommendations.impact: ≤ 973 1–2★/yr on R$220k/yr of orders (upper bound); raises the measured late rate

demoted: Seller quality plan for the 82 'fix-first' sellers (22% of GMV, 87% on-time): ops hygiene, no measurable BRL.

Lane/carrier programme: against a lane-adjusted baseline the 10 worst lanes have only 277 excess late orders/yr (≈57 1–2★ recorded, 20 post-delivery), down from 1,143 vs the network average. No carrier ID exists.

Money on reviews: one extra 1–2★ review is associated with −R$13 of the seller's next-4-week GMV (95% CI −R$62 to R$36): not detectable. Caveat: per the dataset description, Olist sells through the 'Olist Store' on partner marketplaces, so buyers may mostly see the store's reputation rather than a seller's; the seller-week panel may be the wrong unit, so the null is uninformative.

net.interactions: Rec 1 changes how lateness is recorded in stars, so the A/B runs after it ships, never across it. Rec 3 delays the recorded delivery, which delays the star survey and raises the measured late rate. Sizes are upper bounds and not additive.
